newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Brau Union H1 beer sales up, volume down.
newsitem.headline: Brau Union H1 beer sales up, volume down.

text.p: Brewer Brau Union, majority owned by Oesterreichische Brau-Beiteiligungs AG, said on Wednesday group first-half beer sales rose 2.3 percent despite a slight decline in volume.

In a letter to shareholders, Brau Union said it expected to repeat its 1995 result this year although the second half had got off to a slow start. In 1995 Brau Union reported a pre-tax profit of 308 million schillings.
"The second half started with a significant drop in sales, caused by poor weather, declining Austrian tourism and aggressive price competition in the Czech Republic," Brau Union said.
In the first half of 1996 foreign beer sales increased 10.1 percent to 739 million schillings and domestic sales rose 0.7 percent to 3.43 billion schillings.
Sales volume slipped 0.1 percent to 4.01 billion hectolitres, however, due mainly to a 0.9 percent drop in the key Austrian market, where Brau Union moved 2.72 billion hectolitres of beer.
"Lower priced products were most affected. This trend combined with price increases helped boost earnings," Brau Union said.

It reported a significant increase in exports to the former Soviet Union, Germany, Italy and Switzerland but said trade restrictions had a negative impact on exports to eastern Europe, particularly Romania.
New products, like Goesser ICE beer, had helped turn around flagging domestic consumption, Brau Union noted.
The group's workforce fell by 200 in the first half to 4,772.
